1. Heard Sri Virendra Mishra, learned counsel for the petitioner and Sri Ratnesh Chandra for the respondents.
2. By means of the present petition the petitioner has challenged the order dated 18.5.2019 passed by Special Judge, P.C. Act, Court No.5/Additional District Judge, Lucknow in Misc. Civil Appeal No.69 of 2016 whereby the appeal preferred by the petitioner has been rejected upholding he order dated 5.1.2016 passed by Civil Judge (Senior Division), Malihabad, Lucknow who has in turn rejected the application under Order 35 Rule 1 and 2 of CPC preferred by the petitioner.

3. The dispute in the present case pertains to land of khasra No. 267 measuring 17 biswa i.e. 0.215 hectare situated at Village Biharipur, Pargana, Tehsil and District Lucknow.
It is stated that the said land originally belonged to Shri Krishan Hari Saxena who had executed a will in favour of the petitioner bequeathing his movable and immovable properties and his favour.

4. It is further submitted that aforesaid land was acquired by Uttar Pradesh Avas Evam Vikas Parishad in 1971 and the award was also made on 20.9.1974 but no compensation was ever paid to Krishan Hari Saxena or to the petitioner who claims to have succeeded the property after his death and consequently submits that acquisition proceedings had lapsed in view of Section 24(2) of of Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013.

entities.label: ORG

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: The opposite parties asserted their right over the acquired property and tried to interfere in peaceful possession of the petitioner and consequently regular suit No.2397 of 2014 was preferred by the petitioner before Civil Judge (Senior Division), Malihabad, Lucknow for permanent injunction.
In the said suit an application under Order 39, Rule 1 and 2 CPC was also filed seeking to restrain the opposite parties from interfering in the disputed property.

The application of the petitioner was duly heard and considering that the land has been acquired it was held that the petitioner could not establish his ownership of the said land and consequently the same was rejected on 5.1.2016.

5 . The petitioner being aggrieved by rejection of his application under Order 39, Rule 1 and 2 CPC preferred Civil Misc. Appeal No.69 of 2016 before District Judge which was transferred toSpecial Judge, P.C. Act, Court No.5/Additional District Judge, Lucknow.

entities.text: P.C. Act, Court No.5/Additional District Judge, Lucknow
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: It is submitted hat the respondents filed certain documents and objections before the appellate court including papers which according to the respondents indicated that compensation was paid with regard to the disputed property.

The appellate court duly considered the said objections and found that there was material on record to indicate that compensation for the disputed property has been paid and also found that there is no requirement for interference in the order by the trial court declining to grant interim injunction in favour of the petitioner and accordingly dismissed the appeal.

It is further submitted that possession of some portion of the disputed property has already been acquired by the respondents and certain portion of the property is still in possession of the petitioner.
6.

In the present petition both the aforesaid orders, namely order dated 18.5.2019 and 5.1.2016 have been assailed from a perusal of which it is noticed that suit are still pending consideration before the Civil Judge (Sr. Division), Malihabad Lucknow and the present proceedings have arisen only on account of rejection of the proceedings of application preferred under Section 151 CPC.

7. The appellate court after examining the entire facts and circumstances of the case was of the view that the petitioner is not entitled to any benefit of Section 24 of Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013.

sentences.text: The said finding has not been attained finality.

In light of the fact the suit proceedings are still pending and the question as to whether the possession of the property has been taken over by U.P. Avas Evam Vikas Parishad is yet to be considered by the trial court for which purposes it would be necessary to look into the evidence produced by the parties in the suit proceedings.

2 possession of the petitioner and accordingly in the aforesaid circumstances, limited interference is required so as to protect the interest of the petitioner till the decision of the suit proceedings..
8. Appeal has been decided against the petitioner and in favour of the respondents.
We do not find merit in the impugned order upholding the rejection of temporary injunction filed by the petitioner.
We have also noticed that much time has lapsed since filing of the suit, and in case the same is expeditiously disposed off it will reduce further litigation between the parties.
Accordingly, in exercise of the powers under Article 227 of the Constitution the matter requires interference.
9. Accordingly this Court finds that the said suit is at the stage of evidence and the parties agree that the same can be decided expeditiously within six months from today.

Accordingly, without entering into merits of the case or as agreed by the parties the petition is disposed of with direction to Civil Judge (Senior Division), Malihabad, Lucknow to decide regular suit No.2397 of 2014 expeditiously,
preferably within a period of six months in case there is no legal impediment in accordance with law.
The parties shall fully cooperate in the suit proceedings and shall not take any unnecessary adjournment.
10. It is provided that till decision of the suit status quo with regard to the disputed property shall be maintained by the parties.

(Alok Mathur, J.) Order Date :- 29.5.2024 RKM.
